{
  "research_question": "How does mouse navigation performance vary across five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham) when measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "Sham stimulation shows the poorest performance across all metrics: lowest Success rate (0.273), longest Time-to-Target (4.68s), lowest Path Efficiency (0.308), slowest Average Speed (10.74), and lowest AD (0.236)",
    "Combined stimulation yields the highest Success rate (0.780) and fastest Time-to-Target (2.56s), with strong Path Efficiency (0.502) and highest Average Speed (12.83)",
    "Bright Visual Only performs comparably to Combined on Success (0.785 vs 0.780) and Time-to-Target (2.61s vs 2.56s), with slightly higher Path Efficiency (0.504) but lower AD (0.387 vs 0.399)",
    "Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only show intermediate performance, with Success rates around 0.67-0.69, Time-to-Target around 3.0-3.1s, and similar Path Efficiency (~0.43)",
    "AD values are highest for Combined (0.399) and Bright Visual Only (0.387), intermediate for ICMS Only (0.354), lower for Dim Visual Only (0.336), and lowest for Sham (0.236)",
    "Average Speed follows a similar pattern to Success: Combined (12.83) > Bright Visual Only (12.68) > ICMS Only (12.04) > Dim Visual Only (11.97) > Sham (10.74)"
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Success rate: Sham (0.273) vs Combined (0.780) represents a 2.85-fold difference, the largest relative effect across any metric",
    "Time-to-Target: Sham (4.68s) is 83% longer than Combined (2.56s) and 79% longer than Bright Visual Only (2.61s)",
    "Path Efficiency: Sham (0.308) is 39% lower than Combined (0.502) and 39% lower than Bright Visual Only (0.504)",
    "AD: Sham (0.236) is 41% lower than Combined (0.399), suggesting substantially more directed/less variable trajectories under sham conditions—possibly indicating cautious or failed search patterns rather than purposeful navigation",
    "The gap between multimodal/bright visual conditions and unimodal (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only) conditions is substantial, with Success rates ~10-11 percentage points higher and Time-to-Target ~0.5s faster"
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "The data suggest that visual stimulation—particularly bright visual cues—provides substantial benefit for navigation performance, with Combined stimulation offering only marginal additional improvement over Bright Visual Only. ICMS alone provides limited benefit over dim visual cues, and both unimodal stimulation conditions fall well short of multimodal or bright visual performance. The extremely low AD in Sham conditions likely reflects disoriented or non-directed movement rather than efficient straight-line navigation, as evidenced by poor Success and Path Efficiency. These findings indicate that visual information dominates for mouse navigation in this task, with bright visual cues being nearly as effective as combined ICMS+visual stimulation.",
  "limitations": [
    "No statistical tests (ANOVA, t-tests, or non-parametric alternatives) have been performed; all comparisons are descriptive only",
    "Sample sizes vary dramatically across paradigms (Combined n=48,846 vs Sham n=3,505), which may affect precision and representativeness",
    "No correction for multiple comparisons or adjustment for mouse-level clustering (8 mice with unequal contributions)",
    "AD interpretation is uncertain: low values could indicate either efficient straight-line paths or failure to engage in directed search",
    "No information on trial-level dependencies, learning effects, or temporal order of trials",
    "Temperature=0.25 and prompt template may influence LLM-based analysis consistency; replication=1 indicates single run without cross-validation"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct mixed-effects models with random intercepts for Mouse to account for clustering, followed by planned contrasts comparing (1) Combined vs Bright Visual Only to test for ICMS additivity, (2) both visual conditions vs ICMS Only to test visual dominance, and (3) all active conditions vs Sham. Include effect size estimates (Cohen's d or standardized mean differences) and confidence intervals. Visualize distributions with violin or box plots to assess normality and outliers, particularly for Path Efficiency which shows extreme max values (29.8) suggesting right-skew. Finally, examine AD × Success interactions to clarify whether low AD in Sham reflects efficient navigation or failed search behavior."
}
